title: Branch and restore overwrites continue after the safety snapshot fails
reasoning: The pre-overwrite safety snapshot is best-effort: unreadable or unparseable current disk content returns undefined, and snapshotDiskBeforeOverwrite ignores that result. Branch switch, branch creation, and restore then overwrite the document anyway. If Word or cloud sync leaves the file temporarily unreadable/partial, DocGit can replace the only current on-disk bytes without capturing them first, defeating the stated safety snapshot behavior.
reproduction: Track a valid document with two branches, replace the working file with temporarily unparseable bytes, then call switchBranch. commitPath logs a skip, switchBranch still writes the target branch head, and the unparseable bytes are lost.
recommendation: Make snapshotDiskBeforeOverwrite return a success/failure result and abort destructive overwrites when the current file cannot be captured. If preserving unparseable bytes matters, copy the raw file to a rescue file before refusing the branch/restore operation.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The smoke test covers the happy safety-snapshot path with parseable unversioned content, but it never exercises unreadable or unparseable content before a branch switch or restore.
suggestedRegressionTest: In the desktop smoke or a focused service test, create a branch, write invalid bytes to the tracked file, call switchBranch, and assert the operation throws or preserves a raw rescue copy instead of overwriting the file.
minimumFixScope: DocumentService.snapshotDiskBeforeOverwrite and its destructive callers: createBranch, switchBranch, and restoreVersion.
